Six extended policies:

| policy | target_tool (owner) | computes | prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|
| install_ext_reschedule_fee | post_reschedule_fee_05a0220d (agent) | fee_amount | [] |
| install_ext_final_payment | pay_final_balance_37ea441b (user) | payment_amount | ← install_ext_reschedule_fee (value_input, gate fee_total, state) |
| install_ext_trip_charge | post_trip_charge_9239fb96 (agent) | charge_amount | [] |
| install_ext_change_order_fee | post_change_order_fee_b62b1022 (agent) | fee_amount | [] |
| install_ext_permit_handling_fee | post_permit_handling_fee_ee01a5f4 (agent) | fee_amount | [] |
| install_ext_progress_payment | pay_progress_payment_cb1125dd (user) | payment_amount | ← trip_charge, ← change_order_fee, ← permit_handling_fee (all value_input, gate fee_total, state) |

Overlap scan:
- Subjects: four policies write `install_fee_charged` (distinct fee_type per tool: reschedule_fee / trip_charge / change_order_admin_fee / permit_handling_fee); two write `install_payment_received` (distinct status scope: final = status completed; progress = status in_progress; distinct payment_purpose final_payment / progress_payment). No two policies govern the same fee_type or the same payment purpose.
- Triggers / eligibility: final payment is scoped to `completed`, progress payment to `in_progress` — disjoint. The four fee policies each fix one fee type; base eligibility (install_scheduling free-reschedule test, install_visits_and_delays trip-charge outcomes, install_change_orders increase, install_permits_and_haul_away passthrough) is inherited.
- Cross-category read boundaries: reschedule fee reads card (holding tier + card_transactions late fees); final payment reads special (linked order status/total/dates and program `vendor_delay_threshold_days`); progress payment reads card (Project Loan draw end / credit_limit). None writes another category.
- Terminal states: each write is one line on `install_charges` plus `balance_due` update on the contract; no status transitions. No terminal-state conflict between policies.
- Scope partition: the `prerequisite` graph has exactly two connected components — {final_payment, reschedule_fee} and {progress_payment, trip_charge, change_order_fee, permit_handling_fee}; they are disjoint and together cover all six extended policies. With M=2 the natural scope assignment is one component per task; whether `charter_scope` follows it is checked in the closing checklist after the reveals.
- Conflicts found: see `override_declarations` (D-1, D-2, D-3) and `rule_compute_equivalence` (D-4 … D-8).

### rule_compute_equivalence

Method: every `compute_basis` value was checked by script to be a verbatim substring of its policy's whitespace-normalised `rule` (all six: no non-verbatim basis, no compute binding without a basis); the `baseline.rule` of each policy is a verbatim sentence of its rule; then each binding's expression was read against its sentence using the evaluator semantics of `check_compute.py` (SUM/COUNT/LATEST scoped to `install_contract_id = HID`; CFIELD/CPARAM/EXISTS return the **first** matching holding of the customer in that category; XCOUNT over the customer's rows with `MONTHS(date, NOW) < 12`).

Per policy:

- **install_ext_reschedule_fee** — prog_fee/prog_trip, request_registered (LATEST created_at, request_type reschedule, status completed), notice_days (DAYS(created_at, original_install_date)), card_late_fees_12m (XCOUNT card_fee_assessed/late_fee, within 12 months), holds_premier/holds_preferred (EXISTS active variant), job-history counts, billed_contract_price, requested_new_date, move_days, the four share ladders and the single final RND: each matches its sentence. Domain gap: `notice_start_amount` puts `notice_days <= 0` in the 0-day tier, while the rule names only "0 days", "exactly 1 day", "2 days or more"; a negative notice (request registered after the original installation date) has no rule tier (D-8, observation unless a world hits it).
- **install_ext_final_payment** — open_balance, holdback (DAYS(completed_date, NOW) <= punch_list_resolution_days), settlement rate (<= due days / > due + 30), forgiveness (incl. the `> 0` admin-fee guard, numerically equivalent to the rule since forgiving the whole of 0 is 0), materials lateness (> 14 and <= threshold / > 0 and <= 14 and <= threshold): match. Domain gap: the flat bundle tier in compute requires `linked_order_total > 0`; the rule's tier is "completed with an order total below the bundle floor", which includes an order total of 0.00 (a no-charge remake) (D-8).
- **install_ext_trip_charge** — visit_day, occurrence, advance_call, crew_size, staged_materials, result: match on the installation-visit domain. Domain gap: `failed_visit_date`, `absent_occurrences`, `unready_occurrences` filter by visit_outcome only (no `visit_type`); the rule's scope sentence is "an installation or warranty visit", so a measure visit recorded `customer_no_show` would be taken as "the most recent such visit" by compute but not by the rule (D-7). Edge gaps: `staging_days` = 0 when `materials_received_date` is empty (rule has no reading for materials not yet received); `call_gap_days` negative (latest declined request registered after the failed visit while an earlier declined one precedes it) has no rule tier (D-8).
- **install_ext_change_order_fee** — scaled_admin_amount, signing gap, sequence, permit amendment: match, except `change_request_registered` = LATEST created_at over **all** `request_type change_order` requests of the contract with no status or link to the billed change order, while the rule reads "the date part of the change order request's registration" — the request the billed change order arises from (the fee line references "the change order request it arises from"). Where a later change order request exists that was not billed (submitted / declined / withdrawn / lapsed), compute and rule pick different requests (D-6).
- **install_ext_permit_handling_fee** — all six ladders and the permit-size rule match their sentences.
- **install_ext_progress_payment** — uncovered fees, wait, timing, change order collection, financing thresholds match their sentences, with two domain gaps: (a) `loan_draw_end` / `loan_amount` = `CFIELD('card', …, status='active')`, which returns the **first** active card account of the customer, whereas the rule defines the Project Loan as "the customer's active Ridgeline Consumer Credit account that carries a draw period end date"; a customer holding an active revolving card as well as an active loan can be read off the wrong account (D-4); (b) `work_start_date` / `timing_start_date` / `collection_start_date` = LATEST completed installation visit, while the rule reads "the date of the installation visit at which work started"; on a contract with more than one completed installation visit compute takes the last, the rule the first (D-5).

Factor-ladder equivalence (each `factors[].ladder` tier is a rule sentence and a branch of its `decides` binding, and conversely): holds for all 29 declared factors — every tier named in a ladder is stated in prose in the rule with its condition and value/method, and every branch of each `decides` expression is a ladder tier.

### prerequisite_graph

- `prerequisite` present on all six policies (`[]` on reschedule_fee, trip_charge, change_order_fee, permit_handling_fee).
- Every `problem` is an extended policy id of this file, none a base id, none self. Graph: final_payment → reschedule_fee; progress_payment → {trip_charge, change_order_fee, permit_handling_fee}. Acyclic (depth 1).
- Every `policy_source` is verbatim in its own policy's `rule` (script-checked, 4/4).
- `form: state` on all 4 edges, no `fallback_reason` — consistent.
- `resolved_by` equals the depended-on policy's `target_tool` on all 4 edges.
- `kind: value_input`, `gate: fee_total` on all 4; `fee_total` is a binding of both blocked computes (`final_payment.fee_total = SUM install_fee_charged`; `progress_payment.fee_total = SUM install_fee_charged`) and each resolving tool writes an `install_fee_charged` line, so the effect "fee_total includes it" genuinely holds.
- `condition` vs the sentence: (A) final←reschedule: condition "every completed customer reschedule request … that the scheduling rules do not make free is referenced by a reschedule_fee line" — sentence "every customer reschedule recorded on the contract carries the reschedule fee line owed for it": same strength ("owed for it" excludes free ones; a reschedule "recorded" ≈ carried out). (B1) progress←trip: condition covers every `install_visit_recorded` line with customer_no_show/site_not_ready (any visit type); sentence covers "every installation visit … at which the customer was absent or the site was not ready" — the condition is marginally broader (measure/warranty visits) than the sentence; on a contract in status in_progress this differs only if a measure no-show is recorded (observation, world-checked per task). (B2), (B3): condition equals the sentence.
- No authoring-viewpoint phrasing ("in this task", "at the opening", "current world") in any `prerequisite` field.
- PASS, with the B1 scope note.

### prerequisite_sentences

Four-point test on each edge:

| edge | connective | state named in record words | no tool / id / snake_case | strength = condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A final ← reschedule: "The final settlement payment is worked out only after every customer reschedule recorded on the contract carries the reschedule fee line owed for it." | "only after" | reschedule requests + reschedule fee line | yes | yes |
| B1 progress ← trip: "The start-of-work payment is not worked out until every installation visit on the contract at which the customer was absent or the site was not ready carries its trip charge line." | "not … until" | visit records + trip charge line | yes | yes (see B1 note above) |
| B2 progress ← CO fee: "The start-of-work payment is fixed only after every signed change order that raises the contract price carries its administration fee line." | "only after" | change order billed lines + administration fee line | yes | yes |
| B3 progress ← permit: "Before the start-of-work payment is fixed, an issued permit whose fee is passed through at cost must carry its permit handling fee line on the contract." | "Before" | permit_status issued + passthrough + permit handling fee line | yes | yes |

- State form honoured on all four; no fallback to test.
- One write per state: a reschedule fee line can be written only by `post_reschedule_fee_05a0220d` (fee_type reschedule_fee); a trip charge line only by `post_trip_charge_9239fb96`; an administration fee line only by `post_change_order_fee_b62b1022`; a permit handling fee line only by `post_permit_handling_fee_ee01a5f4`. No second candidate write exists in this difficulty.
- Derivation, one reading each: (A) the reader of the final-payment rule learns that every non-free customer reschedule must carry a reschedule fee line; the reschedule-fee rule ("fixes the customer reschedule fee owed for a customer reschedule … that the scheduling rules do not make free … posts as one reschedule fee line … referencing the reschedule request") is the only rule whose result is such a line → post the reschedule fee for the reschedule lacking one. (B1–B3) likewise to the trip-charge, change-order-fee and permit-handling-fee rules, each the only rule whose result is that line.
- Scope caveat (D-9): each "every …" sentence quantifies over all reschedules / failed visits, while the depended-on reschedule-fee and trip-charge rules fix the amount only for "the most recent" reschedule / failed visit. On a world with two or more unresolved items of one kind, the prerequisite cannot be satisfied by any amount the depended-on rule fixes. World-checked per task.
- No rule restates another policy's prerequisite sentence; no rule carries a second wording of a dependency, a tool name or another problem's id.
- Cross-problem orders stated in rules that ground no edge: none found. (The trip-charge visit-day tier "trip charge plus the program's reschedule fee" and the change-order-fee permit-amendment tier read program parameters / base `permit_fee` lines, not lines written by another problem of this difficulty; `permit_fee` ≠ `permit_handling_fee`.)
- Base rule sentences stating cross-problem orders that a tree might rest on: none used; every edge rests on an extended sentence.
- Parallel edges of progress_payment: the trip-charge compute reads no fee line; the change-order-fee compute reads `permit_fee` lines (not `permit_handling_fee`) and change order lines; the permit-handling compute reads `permit_fee` lines, visits and fee **payments**. None reads a line another sibling writes, so the three sibling writes commute (no shared balance, cap or dedup key among them). PASS.

### override_declarations

Sentence-by-sentence against each `base_policy_refs` entry (criterion: the scored quantity).

- **install_ext_reschedule_fee** (refs agg_same_address, cancellation_fees, scheduling, visits_and_delays, change_orders, permits_and_haul_away). install_scheduling: the free-reschedule sentence's "otherwise one install_fee_charged row … posts, referencing the reschedule request" is declared superseded; the fee amount (implicitly `reschedule_fee_usd` via the parameter schema and per_tier) is replaced by the ladder — declared. Every other scheduling sentence (scheduled_only, count increment, Ridgeline-side reschedules free and uncounted, free-notice test) is followed: the extended rule's first sentence keeps free reschedules out of scope. visits_and_delays ("rebooked without any reschedule fee" after an installer no-show): followed (that rebooking is not a customer reschedule). The other refs govern no reschedule-fee quantity. No undeclared override.
- **install_ext_final_payment** (refs payments, completion_and_closure). Declared: install_payments "and the remaining balance is due … subject to the punch-list holdback"; completion_and_closure "while punch_list_open is true the customer may withhold up to punch_list_holdback_pct percent …". Findings:
  - **D-1** (undeclared override, dropped/contradicted branch): completion_and_closure continues, unsuperseded, "and the punch list is resolved within punch_list_resolution_days days of completion, after which the withheld amount is due." The extended late tier ("while the punch list is open after that period, the late punch-list share applies", K late_punch_list_share 0.5) keeps half the holdback withheld after the resolution period, where the inherited base clause makes the whole withheld amount due (holdback 0). Same situation, two answers: base → holdback 0; extended → 0.5 × pct × price. Bears on any task whose world has punch_list_open = true and DAYS(completed_date, today) > punch_list_resolution_days. Demonstration belongs to the task file.
  - **D-2** (unsuperseded cap): install_payments "A payment may not exceed the contract's balance_due at the time it is taken." is inherited; the extended settlement timing adjustment adds +1.5 % of the contract price on a late settlement, which can push the final settlement payment above the open balance. Bears only where the late-settlement tier is hit (or, generally, where adjustments exceed reductions).
  - install_payments deposit / tender / Consumer-Credit posting sentences: followed (bank card). completion_and_closure close-out sentence ("a contract with a balance owed never closes"): the extended allowances reduce the payment without posting a credit, so a contract settled at the extended figure keeps a residual balance and does not close; this does not change the scored payment (observation O-1).
- **install_ext_trip_charge** (refs as reschedule). Declared: visits_and_delays trip-charge sentence, whose replacement drops "subject to install_agg_same_address".
  - **D-3** (residual base cap): install_agg_same_address ("At most one trip charge is posted per job address per visit date across all of the customer's contracts … the one posted is the highest trip_charge_usd among the programs visited") is not superseded and remains in force. Where the customer's other contract at the same job address already carries a trip charge for the same visit date, base says no trip charge posts, extended says the ladder amount posts. World-checked per task.
- **install_ext_change_order_fee**. Declared: install_change_orders "A signed increase posts as an install_change_order_billed row with the next change_order_number and incurs change_order_admin_fee_usd". The superseded clause also covers the billing of the change order itself, which the replacement does not restate (observation O-2: over-broad superseded clause; no task writes a change order, so no scored consequence). The re-quote limit, sign-days and holder-signs sentences are followed.
- **install_ext_permit_handling_fee**. Declared: "and permit_handling_fee_usd as a row with fee_type permit_handling_fee, both on the date the permit is issued" (amount and posting date replaced; the tool posts today). The permit_fee passthrough half of the sentence is followed (the extended rule reads the base `permit_fee` lines). No undeclared override.
- **install_ext_progress_payment**. Declared: install_payments "A progress payment of progress_payment_pct percent of the contract price is due on the day work starts". The added uncovered fees and change order collection are within the replaced quantity. install_payments "A payment may not exceed the contract's balance_due" is inherited — world-checked per task.
- Disguised forms: no anonymous intermediate overriding a base quantity, no 0/1 multiplier on a base-fixed amount (`EXISTS` appears only as a tier condition), no dropped base branch other than D-1. No author note calls the base output a "wrong value".

### factor_ladders

29 factors over 6 policies; every ladder has exactly 3 tiers, pairwise disjoint as stated, fall-through = the policy's baseline for that input, each tier stated in the rule and implemented in `compute`.

| policy | factors (effect) | param / method | multi-source (gate shape) | cross_difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reschedule_fee (5) | reschedule_notice (method), cardholder_courtesy (param), job_history (param), job_size (param), move_distance (param) | 4 / 1 | cardholder_courtesy (card holding × card_transactions), job_history (visit rows of two outcome kinds) | cardholder_courtesy → card |
| final_payment (5) | punch_list_holdback (param), project_bundle (method), settlement_timing (param), change_order_fee_forgiveness (param), materials_lateness (param) | 4 / 1 | project_bundle (status × order_total of one special_orders row — same record), materials_lateness (special order dates × special program threshold) ; forgiveness compound on change order lines × admin fee lines (fall-through fork not compound) | project_bundle, materials_lateness → special |
| trip_charge (5) | visit_day (method), occurrence, advance_call, crew_size, staged_materials (param) | 4 / 1 | none | none |
| change_order_fee (4) | change_size (method), signing_speed, change_sequence, permit_amendment (param) | 3 / 1 | none | none |
| permit_handling_fee (6) | permit_size (method), issue_time, signing_lead, permit_hold, reinspection, permit_payment (param) | 5 / 1 | reinspection (two visit-outcome classes), permit_payment (fee payments × permit lines × date) | none |
| progress_payment (4) | project_loan_financing (param), signing_wait (param), start_day_timing (param), change_order_collection (method) | 3 / 1 | project_loan_financing (card account × install billing line) | project_loan_financing → card |

- Counts per policy within bounds (4–6 factors, ≥2 parameter, ≥1 method).
- Per task (assuming the two components above): component {final, reschedule} has multi-source (cardholder_courtesy) and cross-difficulty (card; special); component {progress, trip, CO, permit} has multi-source (financing, reinspection, permit_payment) and cross-difficulty (card).
- Labels: every `method` factor selects a different computation (sum of two program figures vs a multiplied figure vs the figure; percentage of a base vs flat amount vs none; full collection vs percentage collection vs none; fee plus per-thousand vs scaled vs flat); every `parameter` factor substitutes a multiplier. Honest. Every method tier names a computation the rule states.
- No two tiers of any ladder select the same value or method (checked on the `params`: e.g. premier 0.5 ≠ preferred 0.75 ≠ 1; goodwill 0.5 ≠ repeat 1.25 ≠ 1; same_week 0.8 ≠ long_move 1.25 ≠ 1; prompt −0.005 ≠ late 0.015 ≠ 0; full 1 ≠ mid 0.5 ≠ 0; long 150 ≠ short 75 ≠ 0; same_day_call 0.75 ≠ earlier 0.5 ≠ 1; quick_signing 0.9 ≠ late 1.1 ≠ 1; full_loan 0.5 ≠ partial 0.75 ≠ 1; long_wait 0.95 ≠ short 1.05 ≠ 1; start_day −0.01 ≠ late 0.015 ≠ 0).
- Business reality of conditions and outcomes: the conditions read are ones installed-sales businesses do weigh (notice, card-holder loyalty, prior disruptions, job size, move distance, punch list, bundled materials purchase, prompt/late settlement, change-order size, materials lateness, repeat no-shows, crew size, staging, permit size and issue time, financing, wait, payment timing). Weaker-realism tiers recorded as observations, not RED, because each has a recognisable business rationale: O-3 `signing_lead` on the permit handling fee (a quick-signing incentive / late-signing surcharge on a permit service fee); O-4 `last_day_signing_multiple` 1.2 on a change order signed exactly on its last allowed day but not the day before; O-5 `short_wait_multiple` 1.05 raising the progress share when work starts within 30 days of signing; O-6 `later_permit_multiple` 1.1 when the permit fee line post-dates the change order.
- Baseline note bearing on the final payment (O-7, judged per task): the factor `punch_list_holdback` has baseline `holdback_share 0.0`, consistent with the extended `baseline.rule` (open balance). The base charter's own completion_and_closure — rendered alongside — states a holdback of up to punch_list_holdback_pct while the punch list is open, i.e. the very figure of the extended "full holdback share" tier. A reader who follows the base clause alone reproduces that tier.
